The '''2010–11 Scottish Premier League''' was the thirteenth season of the [[Scottish Premier League]], the highest division of [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]]. It commenced on 14 August 2010 and ended on 15 May 2011. The [[2009–10 Scottish Premier League|defending champions]] were Rangers who retained their championship with a 5–1 win at [[Kilmarnock F.C.|Kilmarnock]] on the final day of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9484609.stm|title=Kilma|work=BBC Sport|access-date=16 May 2011}}</ref>

Twelve teams participated in the 2010–11 season, eleven of which competed in the [[2009–10 Scottish Premier League|2009–10 season]]. [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] was promoted from the [[2009–10 Scottish First Division|2009–10 First Division]].

==Events==
* [[Celtic 9–0 Aberdeen|6 November]] – [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] set a new SPL record for margin of victory in a single match with a [[Celtic 9–0 Aberdeen|9–0 win]] against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/nov/06/celtic-aberdeen-scottish-premier-league |work=guardian.co.uk |last=Murray |first=Ewan|title=Celtic hit nine past Aberdeen in record SPL victory |date=6 November 2010 |access-date=13 November 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101109202155/http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2010/nov/06/celtic-aberdeen-scottish-premier-league| archive-date= 9 November 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>
* 10 November – [[Edinburgh derby]] rivals [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] and [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]] beat the [[Old Firm]] of [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on the same day.<ref name = "edinburgh double"/> Hearts beat Celtic 2–0 at [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]], while Hibs produced a 3–0 win against Rangers at [[Ibrox Stadium|Ibrox]].<ref name = "edinburgh double"/> ''[[The Scotsman]]'' newspaper reported that this last happened in April 1972.<ref name = "edinburgh double">{{cite news|url=http://www.scotsman.com/heartofmidlothianfc/1972-the-last-time-Hibs.6622911.jp |work= Scotsman.com |title=1972: the last time Hibs and Hearts did the double over the Old Firm on the same day |date=12 November 2010 |access-date=13 November 2010}}</ref>

===Referee strike===
{{Main|Scottish football referee strike}}
* 21 November – Scottish football [[referee (association football)|referees]] vote to take [[strike action]], threatening the fixtures scheduled for the weekend of 27 and 28 November.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9214212.stm
|title=Scottish referees vote for strike action
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=21 November 2010
|access-date=22 November 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101122044756/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/9214212.stm| archive-date= 22 November 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> The [[Scottish Football Association]] sourced referees from other [[UEFA]] associations to cover the SPL matches,<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/9216271.stm
|title=SPL matches go ahead despite foreign refs' withdrawal
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=27 November 2010
|access-date=27 November 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101127043830/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/9216271.stm| archive-date= 27 November 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> but all ten [[Scottish Football League]] matches were postponed due to the strike.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/9229449.stm
|title=Referee strike wipes out Scottish Football League card
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=26 November 2010
|access-date=26 November 2010| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101209074954/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_div_1/9229449.stm| archive-date= 9 December 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref>
